bottleneck: Current BCI communication systems transmit roughly 10-40 bits per minute — orders of magnitude below natural speech — because they sample only hundreds to thousands of neurons out of billions, through noisy, low-bandwidth interfaces. The skull attenuates non-invasive signals by 80-90%, while invasive arrays face channel-count, heat-dissipation, and power limits that cap how many electrodes can operate safely. Signal-to-noise degradation in real-world environments further cuts effective rates by 15-30% versus lab conditions. Bandwidth is the fundamental ceiling on what BCIs can express.
current_state: High-density arrays push channel counts into the thousands, but decoding still lags far behind natural communication rates. No roadmap shows a path to speech-rate BCIs with current interface physics.

title: BCI bandwidth orders of magnitude below speech
why_it_blocks: A communication device slower than a telegraph cannot restore natural conversation. Bandwidth caps BCI utility at basic yes/no and slow spelling, not fluent speech — leaving locked-in patients still effectively silenced.
